title: Payment Arrangements Collector Guide — Pre-Suspension Grace Length by Payment Record
content:
For a plan under Payment Arrangements that was suspended, the grace length used to judge whether a pre-suspension installment's grace had run out follows the plan's payment record.

## Rule

The kept installment payments are the installment payments received under the plan less those returned.

- A plan with at least 3 kept installment payments and no missed entry recorded in the last twelve months takes a grace length of 9 days.
- A plan with at least 3 kept installment payments and at least one missed entry recorded in the last twelve months takes 4 days.
- A plan with fewer than 3 kept installment payments takes the type's grace period for its funding method: the type's automatic-debit grace period where the plan is collected by automatic ACH or card debit, the type's manual grace period where it is paid manually.

Missed entries are placed in the period by the date they were recorded. Periods of twelve months are counted in whole months back from the handling date.

## Grid

| Kept installment payments | Missed entries recorded, last 12 months | Grace length |
|---|---|---|
| 3 or more | None | 9 days |
| 3 or more | One or more | 4 days |
| 2 or fewer | Any | The type's grace period for the plan's funding method |

## Worked readings (hypothetical plans)

- 5 installment payments received, 1 returned: 4 kept, at least 3. No missed entry in the last twelve months: 9 days.
- The same plan with a missed entry recorded five months ago: 4 days.
- 3 received, 1 returned: 2 kept, fewer than 3. On automatic debit the grace length is the type's automatic-debit grace period; paid manually, the type's manual grace period.
- Exactly 3 kept installment payments meets "at least 3".
